blocks.content: Quiz: In the fork-based workflow, where do you push your branch before opening a pull request?
Tap an option below to answer:
Directly to the main branch of the original repository
Contributors without write access cannot push to the original repository. That is why forking exists — it gives you your own copy to push to.
Contributors without write access cannot push to the original repository. That is why forking exists — it gives you your own copy to push to.
To a staging branch that the original repository maintainer sets up for contributors
This is not how the standard GitHub workflow operates. In the fork-based model, contributors work entirely within their own fork and open a PR from there.
This is not how the standard GitHub workflow operates. In the fork-based model, contributors work entirely within their own fork and open a PR from there.
To their fork of the repository on GitHub
Correct. You fork the repository, clone your fork, create a branch, push that branch to your fork, and then open a pull request proposing to merge from your fork into the original.
Correct. You fork the repository, clone your fork, create a branch, push that branch to your fork, and then open a pull request proposing to merge from your fork into the original.
To a new unrelated repository they create from scratch
A fork is a connected copy — it maintains the relationship with the original repository needed to open a pull request. An unrelated repository has no connection back to the source.
A fork is a connected copy — it maintains the relationship with the original repository needed to open a pull request. An unrelated repository has no connection back to the source.
